catalogue: Australian residential site preparation and site drainage

ncc_references.relationship: Site preparation, earthworks and site-drainage scope and physical system references.

objects.name: prepared building platform
objects.definition: The shaped and compacted ground area prepared to receive a building's footing or slab system and direct surface water appropriately.
functions: Provide a stable working and founding area
Establish the required site levels below the building
Support site drainage away from the building

cad.placement: Within and around the building footprint
cad.opening: Excavated for footing trenches, beams, pads and services
cad.load: Site substrate supporting the foundation system

notes: This assembly records physical ground and fill geometry; cut and compaction procedures remain process metadata.

objects.name: controlled fill
objects.definition: Selected soil or sand placed in controlled layers and mechanically compacted to form a documented supporting layer beneath or beside construction.
functions: Raise or shape the building platform
Provide prepared support below slabs and edge beams where permitted
Replace unsuitable or excavated material with compacted material

cad.pattern: Placed volume built from compacted layers
cad.placement: Within fill zones of the building platform and below applicable slabs or beams
cad.opening: Interrupted by excavations, services and deepened supports
cad.load: Prepared ground support where the design permits

notes: The ontology does not assign compaction acceptance values; those depend on the applicable provision and project specification.

objects.name: rolled fill
objects.definition: Sand or clay fill placed in layers and compacted by repeated rolling with suitable mechanical equipment under the Housing Provisions method.
functions: Raise and level the slab-support area
Provide compacted fill below construction within its permitted use

cad.pattern: Placed volume built from rolled layers
cad.placement: Below a slab in applicable platform fill zones
cad.opening: Interrupted by footings, services and other excavations
cad.load: Prepared slab support within its applicable limits

notes: Controlled fill and rolled fill are separate NCC construction categories and must not be merged merely because both are compacted.

objects.name: clean quarry sand bedding layer
objects.definition: A level layer of clean quarry sand placed over supporting fill to provide an even surface beneath the under-slab layers.
functions: Level and smooth the prepared fill surface
Provide a bedding surface below the slab membrane
Reduce sharp contact points beneath flexible underlay

cad.pattern: Continuous level layer over applicable fill area
cad.placement: Above fill and below the damp-proofing membrane
cad.opening: Interrupted by beam and footing excavations where applicable

objects.name: unretained fill embankment
objects.definition: A shaped mass of placed and compacted earth that raises the site and is held by its own stable side slope rather than a retaining wall.
functions: Raise or reshape site levels
Create a stable sloping edge to a fill area
Support landscape or building-platform areas where permitted

cad.pattern: Continuous shaped earth volume between crest and toe
cad.placement: At the edge of a raised fill zone
cad.load: Self-supporting earthwork, subject to site constraints

notes: The batter is the sloping face; the embankment is the placed earth mass. Trade usage needs a broader regional check.

objects.name: subsoil drainage system
objects.definition: An underground drainage assembly that collects subsurface water and conveys it away from footings, basement walls, retaining walls or the area beneath a building.
functions: Intercept and collect subsurface water
Reduce water build-up beside below-ground construction
Discharge collected water to a maintained drainage point

cad.pattern: Graded collection runs connected to pits or outlets
cad.placement: Below ground near applicable footings, walls or uphill cut areas
cad.end: Silt pit, sump or approved discharge
cad.opening: Routes around footings and penetrates pits at inlets

notes: Subsoil drainage can change soil moisture and must not be placed by a generic tool without site-specific design input.

objects.name: subsoil drain
objects.definition: A graded underground drainage run, commonly using perforated pipe and surrounding filter material, that collects water from the soil.
functions: Admit subsurface water along its run
Carry collected water to a pit, sump or outlet

cad.pattern: Continuous graded run with branches where designed
cad.placement: Below ground adjacent to the area requiring interception
cad.opening: Connects through pit walls at inlets

objects.name: silt pit
objects.definition: An accessible underground chamber that receives drainage water, allows heavier sediment to settle below the outlet and connects to a downstream drain.
functions: Collect sediment before water enters the downstream line
Provide a transition between drain inlets and outlet
Allow cleaning and maintenance

cad.pattern: Discrete chamber at drain collection or transition points
cad.placement: Below ground with an accessible cover
cad.opening: Has inlet, outlet and maintenance openings

objects.name: drainage sump
objects.definition: A low chamber or pit that receives drainage water for gravity discharge, storage or pumping to a suitable outlet.
functions: Collect water at a low point
Provide storage below connected drain inverts
Permit water to discharge or be pumped onward

cad.placement: At the low point of a drainage system with access for maintenance
cad.opening: Has drain inlets, outlet or pump connection, and access opening

objects.name: underground stormwater drain
objects.definition: A buried solid-wall pipe and fitting run that conveys roof or site stormwater to an approved discharge or on-site system.
functions: Carry stormwater below ground
Connect pits, downpipes and on-site stormwater components
Discharge water without flowing back into the building

cad.pattern: Continuous graded pipe network with branches and fittings
cad.placement: Below ground between collection and discharge points
cad.opening: Connects through pit and tank walls and routes around footings

objects.name: soaker well
objects.definition: An underground chamber that receives stormwater and allows it to soak into suitable surrounding soil as an on-site disposal method.
functions: Temporarily store incoming stormwater
Disperse water into permeable surrounding ground
Reduce direct discharge from the site where approved

cad.pattern: One or more discrete chambers sized and spaced to the site design
cad.placement: Below ground in suitable permeable soil away from affected structures and boundaries as designed
cad.opening: Has stormwater inlet and maintenance access

notes: Suitability and location depend on soil, groundwater and authority requirements; the ontology supplies no automatic siting rule.

objects.name: stormwater detention or retention tank
objects.definition: A tank in a stormwater system that temporarily stores collected runoff for controlled release, reuse or retention on the property.
functions: Receive and store stormwater
Limit or delay discharge according to the system design
Provide water for reuse where configured

cad.pattern: One or more tanks connected into the site stormwater system
cad.placement: Above or below ground at the designed collection and discharge location
cad.opening: Has inlets, overflow, outlet, access and optional pump penetrations

notes: Detention, retention and rainwater reuse tanks overlap physically but have different hydraulic roles; a later drainage pass should split product instances by configured function.
